BNY INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE  
 
Siddhesh Pandey 
B.Tech Computer Engineering, 2023 - 2027 
 
Summer Internship 2026 (On-campus) 
Location: Pune 
Stipend: ₹75,000 /month. 
 
 
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: 
 
1. CS, IT, Electrical, Electronics, EXTC and Mechanical  
2. CGPA: Minimum aggregate 7 CGPA [up to the registration 
deadline, for me it was upto sem 3]. 
 
 
TIMELINE:  
 
Registration: 14 July  
OA: 27 July, 12:00 pm 
Offline PPT: 4 August (10: 30 am) 
OA Result: Just After PPT (25 candidates were shortlisted for interviews) 
Interview: 4 August (after PPT, 1:00 pm) 
Interview result: 4 August (8:00 pm)

ONLINE ASSESSMENT: 
 
There were a total of 8-9 distinct problems and one will get any 4 problems. 
Problem difficulty was from medium to hard level. 
It was a proctored test (video was recorded).  
The platform used was HackerRank. 
Time duration: 2 hour 45 minutes  
Test Starting time :- 12-12.20 PM 
 
The problems were too good and quite difficult. 
I was able to pass all test cases of 3 problems and submitted the test 20 
minutes before. 
Later I saw the solution for the first problem which was very easy but at the 
time of OA i was not able to get that. 
 
The problems were quite difficult if you have not done much DSA or CP. 
I was 100% sure that I will get shortlisted for interviews. 
(Even if you are not sure then also start preparing for the interviews and 
always think positive) 
 
OA problems  
 
OFFLINE PPT: 
 
It was conducted in the mechanical seminar hall at 10:30 pm. 
A total of 8 recruiters were present and the PPT started 30-40 minutes late. 
After PPT ended we got the list of shortlisted students and resumes of 
shortlisted students were collected immediately and were told to get ready 
for the interviews. 
 
I decided to eat something before the interviews from the canteen (always 
be hydrated and eat well before interviews).

INTERVIEW ROUND: 
 
Round 1: Technical round 
Round 2: Project discussion + few HR questions 
The interviews were conducted offline in the college. 
 
Around 1:00 pm the interviews started, my interview started by around 2:30 
pm. 
I was called for the interview at 2:00 pm then waited outside the cabin 
where the interview was already going on. 
I asked the name of the interviewer to the TPO CR present there. 
After around ½ hour of waiting I was called for an interview. 
 
 
Round 1 (Technical, just 2 DSA problem) :  
 
First I greeted the interviewer with a good afternoon, then he also greeted 
me back with “good afternoon Siddhesh” then I confirmed his name by 
asking “Hardik Desai sir, right?”. He was happy and appreciated that I 
remembered his name. 
 
After that he asked me how my day was going, I just answered “it's going 
great”. 
 
Then told me to introduce myself (always prepare your intro very well) 
 
Then he directly started with DSA problems: 
 
He asked me whether I know the sorting algorithm or not and which sorting 
algorithm is best according to me. 
I answered that I don't think we can say that a particular sorting algorithm is 
best, there are always some disadvantages and advantages of every

algorithm and in the majority programming language we use hybrid sorting 
algorithms. 
Then I mentioned that I like the merge sort algorithm. 
 
He directly asked me the time complexity of the merge sort algorithm. 
I directly said that it's nlogn and mentioned the basic idea of merge sort. 
 
Then he asked about quick sort and told me to write the code of quick sort 
on paper. 
First I started explaining while writing but he told me to first write the whole 
code on the paper and then we will do a dry run on some test cases. 
After I finished writing the code I showed it to him and he told me to write 
int main() also and how the quickSort function will be called. 
 
After that he told me to take some examples and do a dry run. 
While doing a dry run, he kept on asking some questions just to confuse 
me. 
 
After that he told me to write recursive code for printing the nth element in 
the fibonacci series. 
At this point I thought we have to print all the numbers from 0th to nth in the 
sequence. 
I asked him whether we directly need to print the sequence in the recursive 
call or return vector of integers. 
He said that there is no need to return any vector. 
 
After I finished writing code for printing the sequence, I showed him and 
then he told me that you need to just print the nth element in the sequence. 
 
Then he told me to write the first few integers in the fibonacci sequence 
and after that I wrote a simple recursive function and mentioned that this 
will have exponential time complexity and we can memorize it further. 
I thought that we would optimize the code but he directly told me that “I am 
happy with this you can go now”. 
He didn’t even ask me whether I had any questions or not.

Round 1 duration was about 25 - 30 minutes for me 
(No CS fundamentals, no good dsa problem, no project discussion in 
round 1) 
Just after my round ended (around 3:00 pm), we were told that lunch break 
is there and everyone can go and eat lunch. 
 
 
Note: 
Few candidates were asked CS fundamentals, design uber and even react, 
tailwind code. 
 
At 3:40 pm I was called for round 2 just after lunch break (I was first to be 
called for round 2). 
 
 
ROUND 2 (Technical + HR) : 
 
This time the interviewer was Vikrant sir (he was the main speaker during 
PPT). 
He asked for my resume and then for the first few seconds he saw the 
resume and then asked me to introduce myself. 
 
After my introduction he directly asked about the project on the resume. 
 
Project discussion included: 
Why did you do this project? 
Features of the project? 
TechStack used? 
How many people worked on this project?

He asked whether it was deployed somewhere or not and asked me for the 
link to the website. 
I told him the link and he opened the website on the tab and saw the 
landing page. 
 
Then he asked me few questions like: 
How do you get the data of the user? (related to my project) 
How is the login feature implemented? 
How is the password stored in the database? 
Name the collections in the database. 
 
After the project discussion he asked, "Have you done AIML?”, to which I 
answered no, then he asked me “why?, some other candidates have done 
AIML, you don’t have AIML in your syllabus?”. 
I answered that till sem 4 we didn't have any course of AIML in college but 
this sem we have ML course and I also mentioned that my main focus was 
to learn Web development and Competitive programming. Now I will start 
exploring AIML. 
 
After this he asked few HR questions,  
Actually after this point it felt like a simple conversation and not like an 
interview. 
 
Then he asked me whether I had any questions or not. 
I just asked one simple question related to interns and internships. 
(According to me, just ask any one simple question not necessary related 
to technology) 
 
Round 2 duration was 30 - 35 minutes. 
My both rounds finished at 4:15 pm and it was mostly confirmed that there 
will not be any round 3.

RESULTS: 
At 4:30 pm a list of candidates who were not selected for round 2 was 
announced. 
Till this point 3-5 candidate’s round 1 was also not started. 
7 candidates were rejected after round 1. 
 
At 6:00 pm round 1 of all candidates were done and a total of 10 
candidates were not selected for round 2. 
 
At 7:30 pm round 2 of all the candidates were done and now a total of 15 
candidates including me were waiting for results. 
 
At 8:00 pm 10 candidates' names were announced, among which 7 were 
selected and 3 in the waitlist (they will get to know about the result later, 
maybe till December, till then they can apply for other companies). 
 
I was among the 7 selected candidates.

TIPS: 
 
DSA:  
I personally have not followed any sheet for practicing 
DSA but still I will recommend you to follow the striver 
sheet since most of the interview DSA questions are from 
striver a to z sheet. 
Regularly participate in online contests and practice 
problems on platforms like Leetcode, GFG and CF. 
 
CS fundamentals: 
Full course: 
OS ,   DBMS ,   CN, System Design 
 
One Shot videos for revision: 
OS ,   DBMS  
 
Practice interview questions on gfg and interviewbit. 
 
Puzzles: Practice on gfg 
 
For previous year interviews and OA problems refer to this drive. 
Practice 5-10 mock interviews with your friends.

Final advice: 
I was selected for the DE Shaw interview but couldn’t clear the 
first round on 2nd August. After that, I wasn’t shortlisted for 
Goldman Sachs interviews despite solving more problems than 
others. I also missed the HILTI OA due to technical issues, and the 
PATTERN opportunity wasn’t something I wanted to pursue. 
Even though an entire month passed without any interview calls, I 
never stopped preparing. I stayed focused with the mindset that 
the next opportunity, I would definitely crack—and on 4th August, I 
finally did. 
I just wanted to say that OA shortlisting can sometimes feel 
random and unfair, and the overall interview process may feel 
disturbing, frustrating, and take longer than you expect. But don’t 
lose hope—I’ve seen people land opportunities at great 
companies even after facing 4–5 rejections. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
-BEST OF LUCK-
